_purpose: Per-prompt answer keys for the 48-question bare-ask suite. Replaces the flat profile-level required_any, which was a single list shared by every question in a profile. That sharing made 'echo the question back' a PASS: e.g. qa-zh required_any contained '行星' while its own prompt was '太陽系有幾個行星？', and longform-zh contained '巴黎'/'文化'/'歷史' while prompt #0 was '請介紹巴黎的歷史、文化和著名景點。'.

_rules.required_any: list[str] — at least one string must appear in the answer (ASCII keys are compared case-insensitively)
_rules.required_all_groups: list[list[str]] — every group must have at least one hit; use when the answer needs two independent components (a claim AND a justification)
_rules.novelty_min: used only when no keyword key is given (open-ended prompts). The answer must contain at least this many characters that do NOT occur in the prompt. Echo-proof by construction.
_rules.length_min / length_max: optional per-prompt override of the profile-level length window
_rules.note: provenance for why this key is shaped this way

_echo_proof: Every key below was chosen so that the prompt text itself does NOT satisfy it. This is verified mechanically by `bare_48.py --selftest-echo`, which feeds each prompt back as its own answer and asserts 0 PASS under the strict ruler.
_honest_limits: longform-zh / writing / the last 3 creative prompts have NO keyword key by design: an open-ended answer cannot be keyword-scored without inventing requirements. They are gated on echo + length + novelty + loop + forbidden instead. Consequence: a long, on-length, non-echo, topically irrelevant answer can still pass. The old flat required_any did not really stop that either (13 shared keywords), and it actively let echoes pass.

translation and qa-zh answers that are legitimately shorter than the profile length_min get a per-prompt length_min override; those overrides are reported separately from the required_any fix so the two changes are not confused.
